相.meaning: A <part>tree</part> and an <part>eye</part> run a window-cleaning business as partners. The tree holds the bottom of the ladder while the eye climbs up to spot every smudge, then they swap. Neither could do it alone, and each thanks the other: the help is <kanji>mutual</kanji>.
相.on: At the end of the day, they share one bar of <sound>soa</sound>p and scrub each other clean.
相.kun: The eye winks at the tree, and the tree winks back with a knot shaped like an <sound>eye</sound>.

隣.meaning: Two houses share one wall. The house on the left flies a <part>pennant</part>; the one on the right keeps a sack of <part>rice</part> on the step. A man on <part>mismatched legs</part> hobbles back and forth between them, borrowing sugar. Side by side for ever, they're <kanji>neighboring</kanji>.
隣.on: He borrows a cup of sugar and gives back a gold <sound>rin</sound>g by mistake.
隣.kun: Next door has a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, an oven full of <sound>na</sound>an and a fish tank like a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

井.meaning: In the village square, <part>two</part> planks lie across a wooden <part>goal</part> frame, making a little grid like a # sign. Peer through the middle: far down, something glints and echoes. Drop a bucket in: it's a <kanji>well</kanji>.
井.on: Down at the bottom, the bucket clangs against an old iron <sound>sa</sound>fe.
井.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' shrieks a frog as the bucket lands on it.

丼.meaning: Look into the square frame of the <part>well</part>: one <part>dot</part> sits in the middle, like an egg yolk. Fill the frame with rice, lay slices of pork on top and crack an egg on top: dinner! It's a <kanji>bowl</kanji> of food.
丼.on: You lift the pork slices out of the pan with a pair of <sound>ton</sound>gs.
丼.kun: A <sound>don</sound>key, a <sound>bu</sound>ll and a fish from the <sound>ree</sound>f queue up for a bowl each.

港.meaning: At the end of the bay, the <part>water drops</part> go calm, and ships crowd in <part>together</part>, tied up side by side. A coil of rope lies on the dock like a <part>cobra</part> ready to strike. Sailors stroll ashore for dinner. The ships are safe in the <kanji>harbor</kanji>.
港.on: The first stall on the dock sells ice cream in a giant waffle <sound>co</sound>ne.
港.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat sells hot <sound>na</sound>an beside a <sound>to</sound>tem pole carved like a lighthouse.

寒.meaning: Under a freezing <part>roof</part>, the water in the <part>well</part> has frozen solid, and <part>one</part> extra plank is nailed over it. A man stands on top with his legs spread like an <part>eight</part>, and each icicle drips a frozen <part>dot</part> on the floor. Brrr! It's bitterly <kanji>cold</kanji>.
寒.on: To cheer up the room, he puts a frozen pink <sound>car</sound>nation in a jar.
寒.kun: A <sound>sa</sound>rdine freezes in the bucket, and a <sound>moo</sound>se knocks at the door asking for a blanket.

傘.meaning: In a downpour, two pairs of <part>twins</part> squeeze under one open <part>umbrella</part>, all four gripping the <part>ten</part>-shaped cross of its handle. Feet stick out, elbows bump, and someone always gets a wet ear. One <kanji>umbrella</kanji>, four kids.
傘.on: When the rain stops, they share an ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae underneath it anyway.
傘.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp and a <sound>sa</sound>rdine swim up the flooded street and shelter under it too.

腐.meaning: In the cellar of the <part>government office</part>, someone has left a parcel of <part>meat</part> waiting for the right form to be stamped. Three months later it's still waiting, green and fuzzy, and the whole building stinks. The paperwork made it <kanji>rot</kanji>.
腐.on: The clerk who sleeps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton by the filing cabinets finally wakes up and gags.
腐.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the clock to complain, and even the cat won't touch the <sound>sa</sound>rdine beside it.
